description: Claude is Anthropic's AI assistant known for long-context analysis, careful writing, and strong coding help across chat and projects.

tagline: OpenAI's flagship conversational AI

description: Gemini is Google's AI assistant with deep Google ecosystem ties, multimodal understanding, and strong research workflows.

name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: AI pair programmer inside your IDE and GitHub

tagline: AI search engine with cited answers

name: ElevenLabs
tagline: AI voice synthesis and cloning

pricingNote: Free plan with 10,000 credits a month and no commercial license; Starter is $6 per month and adds a commercial license, Creator $22, and Pro $99; Scale and Business plans for teams

name: Runway
tagline: AI video generation and editing
description: Runway offers generative video models and editing tools for filmmakers, marketers, and creators producing short clips from text or images.
pricingNote: Credit-based plans on runwayml.com

name: Claude Code
tagline: Anthropic's agentic coding in the terminal
description: Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-native coding agent for reading repos, making edits, and running tasks with Claude models.
pricingNote: Uses Claude subscription or API; see Anthropic docs

name: OpenAI Codex
tagline: OpenAI's open-source coding agent for your terminal
description: OpenAI Codex is OpenAI's coding agent. The open-source Codex CLI reads your repo, edits files, and runs commands inside a sandbox with permission controls, and you can sign in with ChatGPT or use an API key. Version 0.164.0 (October 23, 2026) added reusable /presets prompt slots, inline /model and /permissions controls, terminal image previews, enterprise MCP sign-in, and credential masking for remote sessions. GPT-6.1 Sol became its default model in version 0.161.0 on October 7.
pricingNote: Sign in with a ChatGPT plan or use an OpenAI API key; see openai.com/codex for plan details

name: Google Antigravity
tagline: Google's agentic coding platform across App, CLI, IDE, and SDK
description: Google Antigravity is an agentic coding platform for building with AI agents across an app, CLI, IDE, and SDK. Aimed at developers who want agent-driven workflows inside Google's AI stack.
pricingNote: Free for individuals with rate limits; Google AI Pro and Ultra unlock more capacity

name: Grok
tagline: xAI assistant with real-time X awareness
description: Grok is xAI's assistant available on x.ai and X, oriented toward real-time information and a more direct conversational style.
pricingNote: Available via xAI and X Premium tiers

name: v0
tagline: Vercel's AI UI generator for React
description: v0 by Vercel generates UI components and full pages from prompts, geared toward Next.js and modern React stacks.
pricingNote: Free plan with a 7 message per day limit and deploys to Vercel; Plus starts at $30 per user per month and Business is $100 per user per month

name: Lovable
tagline: Build full-stack apps from natural language
description: Lovable turns prompts into working web apps with UI and backend scaffolding, aimed at rapid product prototyping.
pricingNote: Free plan with 5 build credits a day (up to 30 a month); paid Pro and Business plans add monthly credits, see lovable.dev/pricing

name: Bolt.new
tagline: In-browser AI app builder by StackBlitz
description: Bolt.new lets you prompt, edit, and run full-stack web apps in the browser with StackBlitz's WebContainers.
pricingNote: Free plan with 1M tokens a month and website hosting; Pro from $25 a month and Teams from $30 a month, billed monthly; Enterprise is custom

name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
tagline: Cognition's agentic IDE and agent command center, formerly Windsurf
description: Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf, Cognition's AI IDE. It keeps the full Windsurf IDE with Supercomplete tab predictions, and adds an agent command center for running and reviewing many agents, locally or in Devin Cloud, using the Agent Client Protocol. Plans, extensions, and settings carry over from Windsurf, and Windsurf for JetBrains is still available.
bestFor: managing several coding agents in one place
pricingNote: Free $0; Pro $20 per month; Max $200 per month; Teams $80 per month plus $40 per full seat; Enterprise on request

name: OpenCode
tagline: Open source AI coding agent for terminal, IDE, and desktop
description: OpenCode is an open source coding agent that works in your terminal, IDE, or a desktop app and connects to 75+ model providers, including local models. OpenCode 2.0, announced October 12, 2026, added a shared background server for all clients, background subagents, a Code Mode for tool calls, and an embeddable SDK.
pricingNote: Free and open source; bring your own model provider or subscription, or use OpenCode Zen models

name: Cline
tagline: Open source coding agent for VS Code and the terminal
description: Cline is an open source AI coding agent that runs as a VS Code extension and a CLI. It plans and makes multi-file changes, runs commands, and uses MCP tools, with your own API keys or the Cline provider. Version 4.1.25 (October 16, 2026) began rolling out Cline Cloud sessions, which run a task in a hosted sandbox on a GitHub repo and branch you pick and keep going after you close your editor. It also retries interrupted provider responses up to 3 times and fixes timeouts on long local-model requests.
pricingNote: Free and open source for individual developers; pay only for AI inference with your own keys or Cline credits. Enterprise plan on cline.bot

name: Zed
tagline: Fast open source code editor with a built-in AI agent
description: Zed is a fast, open source code editor with an Agent Panel, edit predictions, and support for external agents such as Claude Agent and Codex CLI through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). Zed 1.25.2 (October 21, 2026) added context compaction and session notices for external agents, new GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5.5 models on Amazon Bedrock, and cut binary size by about 33% on macOS. Zed ships weekly releases.
bestFor: running external coding agents in one editor
pricingNote: Personal plan is $0 with your own API keys or external agents; Pro is $10 per month with $5 of tokens; Business is $30 per seat per month

name: Kiro
tagline: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE, CLI, and web agent
description: Kiro is an agentic coding tool built and operated by AWS. It turns prompts into requirements, designs, and task lists (specs), then implements them with parallel agents, and checks behavior with property-based tests. It runs as an IDE that supports Open VSX extensions and VS Code settings, a CLI, and Kiro Web, and works with MCP, AGENTS.md, and the Agent Client Protocol. Recent releases added Memory across chat sessions in the IDE (October 19, 2026), workspace trust in the CLI (October 20), and MCP tools that can pause to ask for input plus Claude Haiku 5.5 support (October 23). You do not need an AWS account to use it.
bestFor: parallel agents from plan to PR
teams that want AWS-grade admin controls
pricingNote: Free tier with 50 credits; Pro is $20, Pro+ $40, Pro Max $100, and Power $200 per user per month; add-on credits $0.04 each

name: Replit Agent
tagline: AI agent that builds and deploys in Replit
description: Replit Agent helps you create, run, and deploy apps inside Replit from natural language instructions.
pricingNote: Part of Replit paid plans: Core is $20 per month ($18 billed annually) and Pro is $100 per month ($90 billed annually); Enterprise is custom

name: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)
tagline: Google's source-grounded research notebook
description: Gemini Notebook, called NotebookLM until Google renamed it on July 16, 2026, lets you upload sources and chat with them, generate briefs, and create Audio Overviews grounded in your documents. Notebooks sync with the Gemini app, and Google is rolling out a secure cloud computer in every notebook that writes and runs code to analyze data in your sources, starting with Google AI Ultra and coming to Pro users on the web.
pricingNote: Free with a Google account; higher limits on Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra plans, and included in Google Workspace plans

name: Consensus
tagline: AI search across scientific papers
description: Consensus searches academic papers and summarizes findings so you can see what research says on a question.
pricingNote: Free plan with unlimited paper searches; Pro is $20 per month ($12 billed annually) and Deep is $65 per month ($45 billed annually)

name: Elicit
tagline: AI research assistant for literature review
description: Elicit helps researchers find papers, extract data into tables, and speed up systematic literature review workflows.
pricingNote: Free Basic plan with unlimited paper search and summaries; Pro is $49 and Scale $229 per user per month, billed annually

name: SciSpace
tagline: AI research agent for literature reviews and papers
description: SciSpace is an AI research workspace built around SciSpace Agent, which searches the literature, summarizes and compares papers, and drafts reports and manuscript sections from the papers you pick. It also has a Citation Verifier that checks whether your sources support your claims. Agent tasks run on monthly credits, and since October 9, 2026 the Advanced and Max plans include unlimited agent usage with fair-use limits.
bestFor: checking that citations support your claims
pricingNote: Basic is $0 with 100 credits per month; Premium is $20 per month ($12 billed annually); Advanced is $90 ($70 billed annually) and Max $200 ($160 billed annually), both with unlimited agent usage under fair-use limits

name: Scholarcy
tagline: AI summaries and flashcards for academic papers
description: Scholarcy summarizes research papers, articles, textbook chapters, and videos into interactive flashcards that pull out key findings, concepts, and contributions. It highlights important sections, points to related reading, stores references, figures, and tables in a searchable library, imports from Zotero, and exports to citation managers, Excel, and note apps, including one-click bibliographies in Word.
bestFor: building a library of research notes
pricingNote: Free plan limited to 10 summaries (free Article Summarizer allows 1 per day); paid subscription unlocks unlimited summaries, see scholarcy.com/pricing

name: Elorian Glimpse
tagline: Visual reasoning model for images and video
description: Glimpse is Elorian's first model, launched October 16, 2026 as a research preview. It reasons over images and video by zooming into regions, rewatching clips at denser frame rates, and running code to measure what it sees.
pricingNote: API listed at $0.60 per 1M input and $3 per 1M output tokens; chat UI also available

name: Muse Wonder
tagline: Meta's frontier model for coding, agents, and computer use
description: Muse Wonder is Meta's most capable model, launched October 12, 2026 in preview on the Meta Model API and in Muse Code. It is built for complex software engineering and long-running agents, takes text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, and has a 1M token context window.
pricingNote: API listed at $4 per 1M input and $20 per 1M output tokens; Muse Wonder Full requires a Muse Code subscription

name: Claude Duet
tagline: Anthropic's proactive agent that briefs you, works in the background, and asks before acting
description: Claude Duet is a new app from Anthropic where Claude works as a proactive agent, opened as a research preview on October 21, 2026. Built around Claude Opus 5.5, it sends a short morning brief from your connected apps, checks them every few hours, and messages you only when something needs attention. It runs on its own cloud computer with a browser, so tasks keep going when your devices are off, and it can use the 6,000 plus connectors in the Claude Marketplace. It shows you exactly what it will do and waits for approval before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything. Available on iOS, Android, and claude.ai by waitlist.
bestFor: daily briefs across email and calendar
pricingNote: Research preview by waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers; included in the plan and uses its usage limits

name: Ideogram
tagline: Image generation with strong text rendering
description: Ideogram is known for generating images that include readable text, useful for posters, logos, and marketing graphics.
pricingNote: Free and paid credits on ideogram.ai

name: FLUX
tagline: Black Forest Labs image models
description: FLUX is a family of high-quality text-to-image models from Black Forest Labs, available via partners and APIs.
pricingNote: API and partner pricing via blackforestlabs.ai

name: Krea 3
tagline: Fast image editing that keeps products and characters consistent
description: Krea 3 is Krea's new image editing and generation model, released October 15, 2026, with its API opened to every workspace on October 19. Most edits finish in under 8 seconds at native 2K, it takes up to 6 reference images per edit, and it keeps products, labels, logos, characters, and text intact while changing the rest of the scene. It is the default image model in the Krea app and is also served through partners like fal, Replicate, Together AI, and OpenRouter.
pricingNote: Free Krea plan with a daily compute allowance; paid Basic, Pro, and Max plans on krea.ai; API $0.06 per 2K image and $0.03 per 1K image

name: ReSO AI
tagline: GEO and AI search visibility for brands
description: ReSO AI helps brands track and improve how they show up in AI search answers and generative engines. Useful for teams focused on GEO and AI visibility rather than classic SEO alone.
pricingNote: See official site for pricing

name: Leonardo AI
tagline: Creative AI image and asset platform
description: Leonardo AI offers image generation, fine-tuned models, and creative asset tools for games, design, and marketing.
pricingNote: Free tokens and paid plans on leonardo.ai

name: Adobe Firefly
tagline: Adobe's commercially safer generative AI
description: Adobe Firefly generates images and design effects inside Adobe apps, trained with an emphasis on commercial use considerations.
pricingNote: Included with many Creative Cloud plans

name: Kling AI
tagline: AI video generation from Kuaishou
description: Kling generates video from text and images with competitive motion quality for short-form creative clips.
pricingNote: Plans and credits on klingai.com

name: Google Veo 3.1
tagline: Google DeepMind's video model with native sound and dialogue
description: Veo 3.1 is Google DeepMind's leading video generation model, first released in October 2025 and added to BuildStack to fill a gap in the video list. It generates sound effects, ambient noise, and dialogue together with the picture, follows reference images of a character, object, or style, extends a clip from its last second, and builds transitions between a first and last frame, with camera controls and output in 1080p or 4K. Videos made with Veo carry a SynthID watermark. You can use it in Google Flow, which offers Veo 3.1 Lite, Fast, and Quality modes, and developers can build with it on Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
bestFor: short video clips with sound and dialogue
keeping a character consistent across shots
image-to-video with first and last frames
pricingNote: Every Google Flow account gets 50 free credits a day: a Veo 3.1 Lite video uses 10 credits, Fast 20, and Quality 100 (Lite and Fast cost half on Ultra); Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra add monthly credits, and free users may be unable to generate video at peak hours

name: Gemini Omni Flash
tagline: Google's video model you can create and edit by conversation
description: Gemini Omni Flash is the first model in Google's Gemini Omni family. It turns any mix of text, images, video, and voice references into short videos and lets you edit them through conversation while keeping characters and scenes consistent. It launched May 19, 2026 in the Gemini app, Google Flow, and YouTube Shorts. The developer model gemini-omni-1.1-flash became generally available in the Gemini API on August 27, 2026, with 3 to 10 second clips, video extension, first and last frame interpolation, and 360p to 4K output. Google now points Gemini API users here after the Veo 3.1 preview models shut down on October 22, 2026. Videos carry a SynthID watermark.
bestFor: short AI videos from mixed references
editing a generated video by chat
Veo replacement in the Gemini API
pricingNote: Included with Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra in the Gemini app and Flow; no cost in YouTube Shorts and YouTube Create; API billed per Gemini API pricing

name: Seedance 2.5
tagline: ByteDance Seed video model with audio and 30-second takes
description: Seedance 2.5 is the video creation model from ByteDance's Seed team. It generates audio and video together in clips of up to 30 seconds per pass, supports multiple rounds of extension for multi-minute stories, takes up to 30 images, 10 video clips, and 10 audio clips as references in one pass, and offers timestamp-level editing plus green screen and camera perspective edits. It is available in Jimeng AI and Doubao, with API access through BytePlus ModelArk.
bestFor: longer AI video with synced audio
editing specific moments in a clip
pricingNote: Available in Jimeng AI and Doubao apps; API via BytePlus ModelArk; see official site

name: Pika H3 Flex
tagline: Fast open-weight video model with synced audio and up to 12 references
description: Pika H3 Flex is Pika's post-trained version of the MiniMax H3 video model, released October 29, 2026. It generates video with synchronized stereo audio at 480p or 768p in six steps instead of 50, and Pika says a 15-second 768p clip can take as little as seven seconds of model compute. You can combine up to 12 reference images, videos, and audio files in one generation, edit parts of a shot while keeping the performance, and upscale a chosen clip to 1080p, 2K, or 4K. Through the Pika API you can also get five separate audio stems: dialogue, score, SFX, foley, and ambience. The generator weights and inference code are released for you to run on your own hardware.
bestFor: fast video drafts with synced audio
reference-guided shots from images, video, and audio
pricingNote: Available through the Pika API; open weights and inference code on Hugging Face and GitHub under the model license; coming to the Pika app on November 2, 2026. Upscaling and audio stems are Pika-hosted features

name: HeyGen
tagline: AI avatar videos, video translation, and the HeyGen Voice model
description: HeyGen turns scripts into videos presented by stock or custom AI avatars, translates videos into 175+ languages and dialects, and includes a Video Agent and an AI Studio editor. On October 21, 2026 HeyGen opened HeyGen Voice Turbo, the fast mode of its in-house text-to-speech model, to developers through its API, free through November 30, 2026 on a best-effort basis. Turbo works with public voices and instant voice clones made from one recording. HeyGen says Turbo and the full HeyGen Voice model rank first and second on the Artificial Analysis text-to-speech leaderboard, which is based on blind listening tests.
bestFor: text to speech through an API
pricingNote: Free plan with 3 watermarked videos a month; Creator is $29 per month ($24 billed annually), Pro starts at $49 per month, and Business is $149 per month plus $20 per extra seat; the HeyGen Voice Turbo API model is free through November 30, 2026

name: Luma Dream Machine
tagline: Luma Labs AI video model
description: Dream Machine from Luma Labs turns text and images into video shots for concepting and creative production.
pricingNote: Free and paid plans on lumalabs.ai

name: Descript
tagline: Edit video and podcasts like a doc
description: Descript transcribes AV so you edit by editing text, with AI tools for cleanup, overdub, and studio sound.
pricingNote: Free and paid plans on descript.com

name: Sora
tagline: OpenAI's text-to-video model
description: Sora is OpenAI's video generation model available through ChatGPT plans where rolled out, for short cinematic clips from prompts.
pricingNote: Available on eligible ChatGPT plans; see openai.com/sora

name: Jockey by TwelveLabs
tagline: Video intelligence agent that searches and edits your footage
description: Jockey is TwelveLabs' video intelligence agent, generally available since October 15, 2026. It searches video and photo libraries by meaning, explains what happens in each clip, groups footage automatically, and assembles highlight reels or rough cuts. It works inside ChatGPT and Claude or through the TwelveLabs API.
pricingNote: Free plan to start; paid Plus and Pro plans on twelvelabs.io

name: Viggle JST-2
tagline: Explorable 3D scenes, ready-to-animate characters, and motion in seconds
description: JST-2 is Viggle's physics-native world foundation model, released October 19, 2026. It generates explorable 3D scenes in about one second, turns a single image into an animation-ready 3D character with no separate rigging or skinning step, and creates full-body motion from text or video. Scenes are decoded into 3D Gaussian splats that play back in the browser. It is free to try in Viggle's PINOC app and available through the Viggle API and the PINOC MCP server.
bestFor: 3D scenes and worlds from a prompt
full-body motion from text or video
pricingNote: Free trials in PINOC on viggle.ai; API starts with 100 free credits

name: Recursive Flint
tagline: Open local coding model that runs fast on a laptop
description: Flint is Recursive's first model, released October 21, 2026: a mixture-of-experts coding model with 40 billion total parameters and about 2.5 billion active per token, built for agentic coding on local hardware. Recursive says it leads MoE models under 50 billion parameters on SWE-Bench Pro v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and SWE-Bench Verified (74.2%), and generates more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro. Weights are on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0 and work with llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and SGLang, plus Recursive's own rec engine. The model was built largely with Recursive's automated research system.
bestFor: private offline coding on your own machine
local coding agents in OpenCode or pi
fixing bugs and writing tests without API fees
pricingNote: Free open weights (Apache 2.0) on Hugging Face

name: Mistral Large 4
tagline: Mistral's open-weight flagship for agentic coding and security work
description: Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, is Mistral's flagship open-weight model, with open weights released October 29, 2026 after a public preview earlier in the month. It is a natively multimodal mixture-of-experts model with about 1 trillion total parameters and roughly 52 billion active, a 1M-token context window, and text and image input. Mistral calls it the best open-weight model for coding and has trained it for defensive cybersecurity work such as reproducing and patching vulnerabilities. It has three reasoning effort settings (low, medium, and high) and runs in Mistral Studio, through the Mistral API, on OpenRouter, in Mistral's Vibe Code, or on your own servers with vLLM or SGLang.
pricingNote: API $0.70 per 1M input tokens, $0.07 cached input, and $2.10 per 1M output tokens; open weights under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight license (modified MIT; Model-as-a-Service providers need a separate commercial license)

name: Harness by Autonomous
tagline: Open source command center for coding agents across your machines
description: Harness is Autonomous' open source command center for AI coding agents, launched on Product Hunt October 17, 2026. It runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and a dozen other agents side by side in real terminal sessions on your Mac and Linux machines, gives each agent its own git worktree, keeps agents running after you close the app, and links remote machines over end-to-end encrypted connections.
bestFor: running several coding agents in parallel
supervising agents from desktop or phone
pricingNote: Free desktop app and MIT-licensed source; bring your own agent subscriptions and model usage

name: Replica by GitHub
tagline: Open-source AI prototyping that uses your own design system
description: Replica is an AI prototyping tool from GitHub Design, open sourced October 28, 2026. You describe an idea in natural language in the GitHub Copilot app, and Replica builds an interactive prototype that uses your team's existing components, patterns, and documentation. Designers set the guidance, anyone on the team can create and refine prototypes, and you can publish them to an optional self-hosted Replica Hub where teammates leave comments.
bestFor: prototypes built from your design system
pricingNote: Free and open source under the MIT license; you use it through the GitHub Copilot app

name: Lindy
tagline: No-code AI agents for business workflows
description: Lindy builds AI agents that can email, schedule, research, and automate business tasks with connected apps.
pricingNote: Start with $50 in free credits for 7 days, no card; then paid seats from $29.99 per active user a month with 3,000 credits each in a shared pool; top-ups $10 per 1,000 credits; Enterprise is custom

name: Manus
tagline: Autonomous AI agent for multi-step work
description: Manus is an autonomous agent product aimed at completing multi-step computer tasks from high-level goals.
pricingNote: Free plan with 300 credits a day; Pro from $20 a month (4,000 credits) or $40 a month (8,000 credits, 7-day free trial); Team from $20 per seat a month; 17% off with annual billing

name: GPT-6.1 Terra
tagline: OpenAI's fast, low-cost model for computer use and everyday work
description: GPT-6.1 Terra is OpenAI's new fast, efficient model for visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clear writing, released in October 2026 as the successor to GPT-5.6 Terra. OpenAI says it scores 15 points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra on its Agents' Last Exam computer-use benchmark at about one-third the cost, cuts factual errors sharply, and more than doubles GPT-5.6 Terra's score on Terminal-Bench 4.0 for coding. It has a 1,050,000-token context window and supports web search, file search, code interpreter, computer use, and MCP tools in the Responses API. It is available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and in the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-terra.
bestFor: computer use agents that fill forms and act on screens
pricingNote: In ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu plans; API $1 per 1M input and $5 per 1M output tokens ($0.05 cached input), with Batch and Flex 50% lower

name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
tagline: Moonshot AI's open-weight model for coding and long agent tasks
description: Kimi K3.1 Pro is Moonshot AI's flagship open-weight model, released October 23, 2026, with a 1M-token context window. Moonshot highlights coding, 3D creation, financial research, and long-running agentic work, and offers a Highspeed variant that runs two to three times faster. It is available on kimi.ai, the Kimi apps, the Kimi Work desktop app, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API, and Moonshot says full model weights will be published by November 4, 2026.
pricingNote: API $2 per 1M input tokens, $10 per 1M output, and $0.20 cached input (Highspeed $4 and $20); API unlocks after a $1 top-up; in Kimi Code on Plus (Moderato) plans and above

name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
tagline: Fast, low-cost model for agentic work, coding, and computer use
description: MiniMax M3.1 Flash is MiniMax's next-generation Flash model, released October 19, 2026. MiniMax says it runs nearly three times faster and cuts agentic usage costs by 70% compared with its predecessor, with strong results on enterprise automation, software engineering (73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1), computer use (61.7 on OSWorld V2), and cybersecurity tasks. An early version ran anonymously as Space Bunny. It is available through the MiniMax API, M Plan, and the MiniMax Code desktop app, with model weights to follow.
bestFor: low-cost agent workflows across SaaS tools
pricingNote: API $0.15 per 1M input tokens and $0.60 per 1M output tokens on platform.minimax.io

name: Liquid AI LFM3
tagline: Small open-weight models for on-device agents
description: LFM3 is a family of six small open-weight models from Liquid AI, released October 27, 2026, covering text, vision, audio, omni, and two decision models, all built on one 1.7B-parameter base. The text model, LFM3-1.7B, has a 256K-token context window, fits in about 1 GB of memory at 4-bit, is post-trained to run inside agent harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw, and can be fine-tuned on a single GPU. Liquid AI says it is not recommended for agentic coding or complex multi-step reasoning. The models are on Hugging Face, the Liquid Playground, the Liquid AI API, and OpenRouter.
bestFor: private agents that run on a phone or laptop
tool calling with a long 256K context
fine-tuning a small model on one GPU
pricingNote: Free open weights on Hugging Face under the LFM Open License v1.0, which allows free commercial use for companies under $10 million in annual revenue; also on the Liquid AI API and OpenRouter

name: Local Code
tagline: Open source private AI agent that runs on your Mac
description: Local Code is an open source AI agent from the makers of Draw Things, released to everyone on October 28, 2026 after a public beta that began in September. It runs language models on your Mac's own GPU, with Python, Node.js, and a shell built into the app, so it can work through whole tasks on folders you choose: analyzing spreadsheets, writing documents and slide decks, generating images and video, building software, and using a built-in browser. With your permission it can also work with Mail, Messages, Notes, Calendar, and Photos. On-device models include Qwen 3.8 27B (16 GB of memory minimum) and DeepSeek 4 Flash and DeepSeek 4.1 Flash (32 GB minimum), and it works offline. You can also pick a cloud model from Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or an OpenAI-compatible server, which sends your prompts and files to that provider. The agent's tools run inside Apple's App Sandbox, and the source is on GitHub under GPL v3.
bestFor: private agents that run offline on a Mac
working on local files, documents, and slides
pricingNote: Free with on-device models, and bring your own API keys at no markup; optional cloud credit top-ups from $9.99 with no subscription; Teams option for setup, custom skills, and on-prem

name: n8n
tagline: Workflow automation with AI nodes
description: n8n is an open-source workflow automation tool with AI nodes so you can connect LLMs to APIs, databases, and SaaS apps.
pricingNote: Free self-hosted Community Edition; n8n Cloud Starter 20 euros and Pro 50 euros a month billed annually, with no card for the trial; Business 667 euros a month billed annually (self-hosted); Enterprise is custom

name: Make
tagline: Visual automation and AI agents across 3,500+ apps
description: Make is a visual automation platform. You build workflows, called scenarios, and AI agents by prompting, dragging and dropping, or from an AI chat such as Claude or ChatGPT through the Make MCP server, then connect them to more than 3,500 apps or any service with an API. You can add JavaScript or Python where you need it, and Make shows every running workflow in one view. It is used by over 500,000 teams, according to Make.
bestFor: AI agents with tools and limits you set
automations you can build from a chat
pricingNote: Free plan with 1,000 credits a month, no card and no time limit (most actions use 1 credit); paid Core, Pro, and Teams plans add credits, and Enterprise is custom

name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
tagline: Microsoft's no-code builder for agents, workflows, and apps
description: Copilot Studio is Microsoft's platform for building custom agents, workflows, and apps with no code, using natural language or a visual designer. Agents can answer questions, take actions, or run business processes on their own, connect through more than 1,500 prebuilt connectors and MCP servers, and hand work to each other in multi-agent setups. You can publish them to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, SharePoint, websites, and other channels, with Microsoft Entra ID security, Purview audit logs, and dev, test, and production release controls. It includes what was formerly Power Virtual Agents.
bestFor: mixing agent steps with classic workflows
pricingNote: Pay as you go at $0.01 per Copilot Credit through an Azure subscription, or $200 a month (billed annually) for a tenant pack of 25,000 credits; prepaid plans save up to 20%; agents used in Microsoft 365 Copilot are included for licensed users; free trial for individuals

name: Gumloop
tagline: No-code AI agents that work across your apps
description: Gumloop lets teams build AI agents that connect to their apps, run on triggers, and hand work to other agents. Gumball, launched September 3, 2026, is a personal agent in every Gumloop account that runs in the cloud, triages email, preps meetings, and picks a model for each task. Release 12.5.0 (October 19, 2026) let agent-built dashboards and apps call AI models, improved browser sign-ins and form filling, and added a trigger for new Slack channel members.
pricingNote: Pro starts at $37 per month with a 14-day free trial and 20k credits per month; Enterprise is custom pricing

name: Relevance AI
tagline: Build and run teams of AI agents for sales, support, and ops
description: Relevance AI is a platform for building AI agents and multi-agent workforces that run business processes such as account research, meeting prep, CRM updates, and support triage, connected to more than 1,000 apps. Invent 2.0, launched September 29, 2026, is a built-in agent that works like a solutions engineer: it interviews you about a process, builds the agents, tools, and integrations, sets tests before anything goes live, then watches production runs and proposes fixes when quality drops. Nothing goes live until a person publishes it, and every change is a named version you can roll back.
bestFor: multi-agent workforces for sales and support teams
building agents by describing a process
pricingNote: Pro $19 a month billed annually ($29 monthly) with 2,500 Actions a month; Team $234 a month billed annually ($349 monthly) with 7,000 Actions; Enterprise is custom; AI model costs are passed through at cost as Vendor Credits, or bring your own API keys; the Free plan is retired

name: AgentSpot by ThoughtSpot
tagline: ThoughtSpot's multiplayer AI for building and sharing work agents
description: AgentSpot, launched by ThoughtSpot on October 22, 2026, lets anyone describe an agent, a recurring workflow, or an interactive app in plain language, then share it across the company. Agents run on ThoughtSpot's semantic layer, connect to tools such as Slack, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and GitHub, keep company, agent, and user memory, and log every action for audit. Usage is measured in DO credits: one per agent conversation, workflow run, or app load.
bestFor: scheduled business workflows on company data
pricingNote: Free plan with no time limit and no card: unlimited agents and users plus a weekly allowance of conversations, workflow runs, and app sessions; paid Fleet plan for more usage

name: Velozity
tagline: Multiplayer AI office for teams and agents
description: Velozity is a shared workspace where teams and AI agents work together in a multiplayer AI office. Built for collaborative agent workflows rather than single-user chat.
pricingNote: Free to start; see official site for plans

name: Mercury 3 by Inception
tagline: Diffusion LLM at 1,000+ tokens per second for fast agents
description: Mercury 3 is Inception's diffusion-based language model, launched October 19, 2026. Inception reports 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs, a 1M-token context window, and quality on par with speed-optimized frontier models. It is built for latency-sensitive work such as browser agents, real-time search, voice and chat support, and tutoring, and it is available through an OpenAI-compatible API on the Inception platform, OpenRouter, Baseten, and Vercel AI Gateway.
pricingNote: API list price $0.20 per 1M input and $0.70 per 1M output tokens, 50% off at launch; 100 million free API tokens to try

name: Otter.ai
tagline: AI meeting notetaker with chat and task agents
description: Otter.ai records and transcribes meetings with speaker identification, then writes summaries you can search across every conversation. Its AI Chat 2.0, rolling out on web and desktop in October 2026, adds a Work mode that completes multi-step tasks through connected apps such as Jira, Notion, Google Drive, and Gmail. An Otter MCP server also lets Claude, ChatGPT, and other assistants search your meeting transcripts.
pricingNote: Free Basic plan; paid Pro and Business plans on otter.ai

name: Fireflies.ai
tagline: AI meeting notetaker for transcripts, summaries, and search
description: Fireflies joins Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and other calls to record, transcribe, and summarize them, and it also transcribes uploaded audio and video files (MP3, MP4, WAV, M4A). It supports 100+ languages and speaker recognition, and adds searchable notes, action items, AI Skills that run on your meetings, Voice Agents that hold calls for you, and an MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT, and Devin. Fireflies is SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant and says it does not train AI models on customer data.
bestFor: sending call notes to CRMs and Slack
pricingNote: Free plan; Pro is $10 and Business $19 per seat per month billed annually ($18 and $29 billed monthly); Enterprise is $39 per seat per month, annual only

name: Mistral Voxtral 3
tagline: Transcription, expressive speech, and a real-time voice agent SDK
description: Voxtral 3 is Mistral's new family of speech models, released October 20, 2026. It includes transcription for 50+ languages with speaker diarization, context biasing, and end-of-turn detection, a realtime transcription model under 500 ms latency, and a text-to-speech model with emotion, pacing, and emphasis control across 35+ languages and 50+ dialects. A voice agent SDK built on LiveKit combines listening, reasoning, tool calling, and speaking in one streaming pipeline, over SIP or WebRTC. It runs on Mistral's EU, US, or global API or on your own infrastructure.
pricingNote: API from $0.0035 per minute for transcription; TTS $13 per 1M characters; voice agent API from $0.04 per minute

name: AssemblyAI-TTS-1
tagline: Low-latency text to speech built for voice agents
description: AssemblyAI-TTS-1 is AssemblyAI's text-to-speech model for voice agents, generally available since October 27, 2026. It streams audio in about 90 ms in production and has unlimited concurrency on pay-as-you-go with no annual contract. It ships with more than 4,000 voices, instant voice cloning once you confirm the speaker's permission, word timestamps, and a choice of US or EU processing. At launch it speaks English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Portuguese, and AssemblyAI provides reference agents for LiveKit and Pipecat.
pricingNote: $15 per 1M characters, pay as you go, with every voice, language, and voice cloning included; volume pricing for committed usage

name: Phonic-1
tagline: Speech-to-speech voice agent model that acts while the caller talks
description: Phonic-1 is a speech-to-speech model from Phonic for voice agents, released October 29, 2026. It hears the caller's audio directly and answers in speech, with under 600 ms from speech in to speech out, and Phonic says it is the only speech-to-speech model that can call tools while the caller is still talking. It handles interruptions and turn-taking on noisy lines, speaks more than 50 languages with switching mid-conversation in the same voice, and pronounces URLs, emails, and codes accurately. You build on it with the API, TypeScript and Python SDKs, a CLI, or a no-code agent builder, and Phonic offers SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA with a BAA, and zero data retention.
bestFor: phone voice agents that call tools
pricingNote: One price per minute starting at $0.07, with no LLM pass-through or per-token charges

name: Zapier
tagline: No-code automation across thousands of apps
description: Zapier connects apps with Zaps and AI features so non-developers can automate handoffs between SaaS tools.
pricingNote: Free plan with 100 tasks a month and two-step Zaps; Professional starts at $19.99 per month billed annually ($29.99 monthly); Team and Enterprise for organizations; 14-day Professional trial with no card

name: IBM Granite Speech 5.0
tagline: Open speech models for accurate, fast transcription and translation
description: Granite Speech 5.0 is IBM's latest open speech collection, released October 21, 2026. The new granite-speech-5.0-2b model transcribes English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, translates to and from English, supports keyword lists of up to 2,000 terms, and ranks second among open-weight models on the Open ASR Leaderboard's average English word error rate. The updated 470M Turbo CTC model adds multilingual transcription with native punctuation and runs about 1.6 times faster than before, and the refreshed 4.1 2B Plus model improves speaker attribution and timestamps for meetings and calls. All are Apache 2.0.
pricingNote: Free open weights (Apache 2.0) on Hugging Face

name: Fish Audio Drama 3
tagline: Text-to-speech you direct in plain language
description: Drama 3 is Fish Audio's most emotive text-to-speech model, released publicly October 13, 2026. You direct each line in plain words, add sighs, laughs, and pauses exactly where you want them, and scope effects like a whisper to specific words. It speaks 83 languages, handles multi-speaker scenes, and is available on fish.audio, the Fish Audio mobile apps, the API, and as open weights on Hugging Face.
pricingNote: Creator plans on fish.audio; API launch price $10 per 1M characters through November 12, 2026 ($50 list); open weights free for commercial use under US$500K annual revenue

name: Gradium Phonon
tagline: Open-source text to speech that runs on your own device
description: Phonon is an open-source on-device text-to-speech model from Gradium, the voice AI company founded by the cofounders of the Kyutai research lab, released October 21, 2026. It comes in 31M and 40M parameter versions, small enough to ship inside a mobile app or load in a browser tab, and speaks English, French, German, Spanish, and Portuguese in one model. Speech is generated locally, so text and audio stay on the device. It includes ready-made voices, speed control, and integrations for Rust, Python, Swift, and the browser through WebAssembly.
bestFor: private text to speech inside apps
speech in the browser and on embedded hardware

Nothing publishes until someone merges, and it learns your team's tone and update habits from the PRs you review.
